name: Second Hand High
description: Second Hand High: 7-card stud variant where at showdown the second-highest hand wins the pot. Same deal and betting as 7-card stud; if all but one player fold, the survivor wins. USA; dealer's choice.

overview.description: Second Hand High: 7-card stud variant where at showdown the second-highest hand wins the pot. Same deal and betting as 7-card stud; if all but one player fold, the survivor wins. USA; dealer's choice.

history.origins: American 7-card stud variant in which the second-highest hand at showdown wins the pot. Encourages staying in with second-best draws.
timeline: Present: Played in mixed and novelty games

setup.players: A standard 52-pack is used and from 2 to 8 players can take part. The game is best for 5 to 7 players. When 8 play there is the problem that the cards may run out towards the end of the deal.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the second-best hand at showdown; the second-highest hand takes the entire pot.
rules.gameplay: Deal and betting as in 7-card stud. At showdown, the second-highest five-card hand wins the pot. If all but one fold, that player wins. If there is a tie for first, none of those hands wins and the next highest hand takes the pot; if there is a tie for second, the equal hands split the pot.
keyRules: Second-highest hand at showdown wins the pot
Tie for first: next highest wins; tie for second: split pot

strategy.basic: Playing for second place is viable; don't fold marginal hands when the pot is large.
strategy.intermediate: Estimate whether you're competing for first or second; size bets accordingly.
strategy.advanced: Multi-way pot strategy: sometimes call to try for second rather than win.

variations.emptyOverridesReason: No documented variations; add when found in sources.

scoring.description: The second-highest hand at showdown wins the entire pot; ties for second split the pot.
scoring.winCondition: Win the pot with the second-best hand at showdown; the second-highest hand takes the pot.
